messages.subject: Re: mirt.model() function
parts:
See the example in ?mirt.model when passing names to the syntax. You also need to include the names of the variables under use, otherwise the function doesn't know which variables you are referring to. Typically I just use numeric locations though, because it saves from knowing the variable names. 

In the future, I may just allow all estimation functions to accept a string instead of a mirt.model() object, that way this issue can be handled better and mirt.model() need not be called at all. E.g., something like this in the future will be possible:

model <- 'F1 = p1-p5
                F2 = p6-p10
                COV = F1*F2'
mod <- mirt(data, model)

which seems to have a more lavaan-like flavour for defining models. 

Also, I forward your message to the mirt-package forum, which is a good place to find and ask questions (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/mirt-package). Cheers.

Phil
